title: Costco's Kirkland cold and flu medicine recalled; FDA says key ingredient 'not effective'
excerpt: The FDA recalled 8,640 boxes of Costco's Kirkland Severe Cold & Flu medicine for quality-control issues, saying its decongestant ingredient is 'not effective.'
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration recalled 8,640 boxes of Costco's Kirkland Severe Cold & Flu Plus Congestion Day and Night packs last week, pulling a popular store-brand cold medicine from shelves over quality-control issues.

The recall covers boxes with lot numbers P139953 or P139815 and an August 2026 expiration date, according to the FDA notice reported by Fox News Digital. It is a Class II recall, the FDA's category for products that could cause temporary or reversible health effects.

The product's listed active ingredients are acetaminophen, dextromethorphan, guaifenesin and phenylephrine. The FDA said the recall was related to quality-control issues, and the agency's notice pointed to deviations in manufacturing practice.

The recall lands as the FDA moves against the decongestant itself. After "extensive review," the FDA concluded that oral phenylephrine is "not effective" as a nasal decongestant, and in early November the agency proposed banning oral phenylephrine as an over-the-counter nasal decongestant.

Pharmacist Katy Dubinsky, founder and CEO of Vitalize, told Fox News Digital the recall most likely occurred because of deviations from current good manufacturing practice, the federal standards for how drugs are made and checked.

Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News' senior medical analyst, said he agrees with the pushback against the ingredient. He noted that oral phenylephrine has been shown ineffective against cold and flu symptoms in its oral form, except at a dose that carries some heart toxicity and can lead to palpitations and arrhythmia.

Shoppers who bought the Kirkland Severe Cold & Flu packs can check the lot number printed on the box against the recalled lots. The recalled product should not be used, and the FDA's recall notice is the place to confirm whether a specific box is covered.
